findings.title: Removing the write lock around BuildIndex allows concurrent builds for the same key
findings.body: BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the whole function, serializing all index builds. Now only the final cache write is locked. Two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource (e.g. a watch event triggering getOrCreateIndex while the startup indexing is still building, or two concurrent searches for the same key) will both call bleve.New on the same directory path (b.opts.Root/namespace/resource.group). bleve.New fails if the path already exists, so the second build errors out; for the mem-only case both builds complete and one index is silently discarded while duplicating all the indexing work and double-counting the IndexTenants metric. Consider per-key locking (e.g. an in-flight map or singleflight) rather than dropping the lock entirely.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads b.cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs iterates b.cache with no lock while BuildIndex now writes to the map under b.cacheMu. Previously builds held the lock for their whole duration, which reduced the window; with the finer-grained locking, concurrent builds (startup indexing workers, watch-event driven builds) can write to the map while TotalDocs ranges over it, which is an unsynchronized map read/write and will trigger a fatal 'concurrent map iteration and map write' panic. TotalDocs is called from searchSupport.init logging, so this is reachable. Take b.cacheMu.RLock() in TotalDocs.

findings.title: Shared err and counter written from concurrent errgroup goroutines
findings.body: Inside the errgroup in searchSupport.init, each goroutine assigns to the enclosing `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increments the shared `totalBatchesIndexed` counter. With initWorkers > 1 these are unsynchronized writes from multiple goroutines: a data race, and `err` is also read after group.Wait() (line 195), so a failure in one namespace can be masked or an unrelated error reported. Use a goroutine-local `err :=` and an atomic/locked counter.

findings.title: NewResourceServer leaks the server context and background goroutines when Init fails
findings.body: s.Init(ctx) is now called in the constructor, but on error the function returns nil without calling the cancel func created at line 229. Any goroutines already started by the search watcher (searchSupport.init starts a watch goroutine on context.Background()) and by the backend poller keep running, and the cancelable context is never released. Call cancel() (and ideally s.Stop) before returning the error.

findings.title: Stop() no longer has any effect on request handling since Init checks were removed
findings.body: Stop sets s.initErr to 'service is stopping'/'service is stopped' as a guard, but every request handler's `if err := s.Init(ctx)` check was removed in this PR. After Stop, Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/blob calls will proceed against a cancelled context and a stopped backend instead of returning a clear 'service is stopped' error. Either add an explicit stopped/served state check in the handlers or drop the now-dead initErr mutation in Stop.

findings.title: Postgres path of the storage-server integration test is skipped without a tracking issue
findings.body: The only integration coverage for running the storage server target with Postgres is now unconditionally skipped with a 'works locally' comment. Since this PR changes when unified storage initialization happens (now during server construction), this is exactly the path that would catch startup regressions on Postgres. At minimum reference a tracking issue so the skip does not become permanent.
